description: Language-neutral parity catalog for the dispatcher-facing guardrail (bin/lib/guardrail.py main_cli/gate/_log <-> cli/src/core/guardrail.ts). test/run_core_parity.py builds a fixture vault, then for each 'gate' invocation runs the binary's --core-gate <verb> <args...> and python3 <vault>/bin/lib/guardrail.py <verb> <args...> against SEPARATE copies of the vault (isolated .logs), comparing exit code + stdout + stderr byte-exact AND the appended audit-log line (timestamp shape asserted, remainder after the first tab byte-compared). Fixture grammar additions over resolver.json (additive): verbs[].cmd sets a verb's cmd.json CONTENT (object -> json.dumps, string -> written raw for a malformed-JSON fixture); top-level plugins_lock writes plugins/plugins.lock.json (object -> dumped, string -> raw). Invocation shape: {compare:'gate', verb, args?:[...]}.

cases.name: engine-verb-risks
cases.rationale: Every gate() risk branch on engine verbs: declared read/safe_write allow; confirm blocked without --yes and cleared by --yes AND -y separately; deny refused (and deny beats --dry-run); undeclared risk defaults to confirm two ways (cmd.json without a risk key, and run.py-only with no cmd.json); malformed cmd.json swallowed to null -> default confirm; the --dry-run downgrade fires only when cmd.json declares dry_run:true AND risk is confirm/safe_write, and is a no-op on a plain read and on an undeclared-dry-run confirm verb.

cases.name: plugin-trust-ceiling
cases.rationale: Trust ceiling (Part 2.2) via resolver source_of + plugins.lock.json: an untrusted pack (lock entry without trusted) caps read/safe_write up to confirm and blocks the --dry-run downgrade; an explicitly trusted pack (trusted:true) keeps its declared risk and allows the downgrade; a pack with NO lock entry (user-placed) gets no ceiling. Proves the cap is driven by the lock, not the pack's self-declared cmd.json risk.

cases.name: malformed-plugins-lock
cases.rationale: A malformed plugins.lock.json is swallowed to an empty map on BOTH sides (Python bare except, TS JSON.parse catch), so no verb is capped and the pack verb runs at its declared risk -> allow. Proves the log/ceiling read never crashes the gate on a corrupt lock.

cases.name: did-you-mean
cases.rationale: main_cli unknown-verb path: difflib.get_close_matches(verb, sorted(known), n=3, cutoff=0.6) with exit 4. Near-miss with two candidates pins ordering (captur -> capture, cap; stas -> stash, status), near-miss with one candidate (serch -> search), and a far-miss (xyzzy) falls back to the ' (run: plainkeep help)' hint. Unknown path returns before _log, so no audit line is written (both logs empty).

cases.name: arg-edge-cases
cases.rationale: Byte-exact stdout/stderr/log across the run.md D5 arg shapes — empty string, spaces, Unicode, embedded tab, embedded newline — on a confirm verb (args echoed in the re-run remediation AND the audit line) and a read verb (args echoed only in the audit line, no stderr). Exercises the field-guide rule: args compared positionally/byte-exact, never through a sorted set, and the log comparison's split('\t', 1) survives a tab/newline inside an arg.
